articles.title: Audio before the socket is ready: queueing WebSocket messages until the session says so, and a final transcript with a deadline
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I'm the developer of Bolo, and this post is published from my account. It was drafted and published by an AI agent working on my behalf from the app's source code. Bolo (search "Bolo AI" o…
articles.body: Disclosure: I'm the developer of Bolo, and this post is published from my account. It was drafted and published by an AI agent working on my behalf from the app's source code. Bolo (search "Bolo AI" on Google Play) can stream a voice take to a transcription service over a WebSocket while you are still speaking. The client class is under 300 lines, and three small decisions in it are worth writing down, because each one fixes a bug that looks like "it works on my network". 1. "Socket open" is not "session ready" OkHttp calls onOpen as soon as the WebSocket handshake completes. The server, though, still has to set up the transcription session, and it announces that with its own message ( session.ready , or session.created / session.updated on the other protocol the class speaks).

articles.title: Your Chat History Is Not a Prompt Library: A 3-Layer System for Solo Operators
articles.excerpt: Ask a solo operator where their best prompts live, and you get one of three answers: in a chat with myself, in a note on my phone, or "I just remember the good ones." All three mean the same thing: no…
articles.body: Ask a solo operator where their best prompts live, and you get one of three answers: in a chat with myself, in a note on my phone, or "I just remember the good ones." All three mean the same thing: nowhere. That is fine until the work has a deadline attached to it. The quote goes out on Tuesday. The reminder email goes out on the 8th. The intake form goes to a client who is already slightly annoyed. At that point, a prompt you cannot find is a prompt you rewrite, and the rewrite is never quite the same as the one that worked. Different sentence order, one detail dropped, a tone ten percent sharper than last time. The output drifts, and you cannot tell whether the drift came from your prompt, the model, or the input.

articles.title: What's New in React 19: A Guide to the Latest Updates
articles.excerpt: What's New in React 19 React 19 introduces several key features and improvements, including stable Server Components, automatic memoization via the React Compiler, and streamlined form handling. React…
articles.body: What's New in React 19 React 19 introduces several key features and improvements, including stable Server Components, automatic memoization via the React Compiler, and streamlined form handling. New Features and Improvements React Compiler: Automatically optimizes and memoizes components during build time, removing the need to manually write useMemo and useCallback hooks. Stable Server Components & Actions: Allows components to run on the server and interact with databases directly, reducing the amount of JavaScript sent to the user's browser. Simplified Form Handling: Built-in action props on forms and new hooks ( useActionState , useOptimistic , and useFormStatus ) eliminate repetitive boilerplate for loading states and submissions.

articles.title: Weekday and weekend limits in my free Android app blocker, and a usage bug that only showed up after updates
articles.excerpt: I build Ripple, a free Android app for limiting your own phone use or setting limits on a child's phone. No account, no ads, and rules stay on the phone. This post covers two recent releases: v0.1.25…
articles.body: I build Ripple, a free Android app for limiting your own phone use or setting limits on a child's phone. No account, no ads, and rules stay on the phone. This post covers two recent releases: v0.1.25 added per-weekday daily limits, and v0.1.26 fixed today's usage being counted too high on some phones after an update install. Why per-weekday limits Until v0.1.25 a daily limit was one number for every day. People kept asking for something different on weekends. An adult might want 30 minutes of short videos on workdays and 90 on Saturday. A parent might want a game at 0 minutes on school days and an hour on weekends. On an app's limit page there is now a "By weekday" option. Each day from Monday to Sunday gets its own value, which can be "No limit" or 0 min (blocked all day).

articles.title: The Ten Minutes Before You Hit Publish: Lessons from Building RankPilot AI
articles.excerpt: I make Shorts myself. Story channels, comedy series — filmed, edited, and uploaded from one phone, mostly late at night, mostly tired. And for a long time my upload routine was the same small mess eve…
articles.body: I make Shorts myself. Story channels, comedy series — filmed, edited, and uploaded from one phone, mostly late at night, mostly tired. And for a long time my upload routine was the same small mess every time. I typed the first title that came into my head. I left the description box almost empty because the video was already late. I grabbed three tags in a hurry, published, and then blamed the algorithm when nothing moved. The algorithm was not fully innocent. But my packaging was not innocent either. RankPilot AI is the app I built to give those last ten minutes before publishing the attention they deserve. It is an upload companion: it helps you prepare a video's title, description, and tags properly, in one sitting, before the video goes out. This is what building it taught me.

articles.title: CallCue, for the smile that words don’t carry
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Presage SmartSpectra SDK Challenge. “Mum, I’m coming home.” There is a smile before the reply. Imagine Nora, a blind daughter, calling her mum. She knows that voice by hea…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Presage SmartSpectra SDK Challenge . What I Built “Mum, I’m coming home.” There is a smile before the reply. Imagine Nora, a blind daughter, calling her mum. She knows that voice by heart. But the smile, the part that happens before either person says another word, belongs in the conversation too. That imagined moment is the heart of CallCue , a one-to-one calling prototype built to give blind and low-vision callers a little more facial context through short, private spoken cues. Not a dashboard to watch. Not another person talking over the call. A brief description, such as “They look happy,” with room for the conversation to continue. A call, not a setup project One person starts a call and shares the link. The other person joins in their browser.

articles.title: GrapheneOS just built its own RCS messaging app that makes Google Messages unnecessary
articles.excerpt: It's a proof-of-concept app right now, but the eventual goal is a standalone implementation for supported carriers.
articles.body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR GrapheneOS has built a proof-of-concept RCS messaging app with end-to-end encryption and compatibility with Google Messages and iOS. The experimental app supports typing indicators, read receipts, reactions, and media and file sharing. The initial implementation will still depend on sandboxed Google Play, but won’t require Google Messages. The eventual goal is a standalone implementation for supported carriers. The RCS functionality will effectively be exclusive to GrapheneOS. GrapheneOS is making progress on one of its most anticipated messaging features, and it could eventually let users enjoy RCS without relying on Google Messages.
